# Atomic write of aggregates and consumer offset in one Kafka transaction

> Sends minute aggregates and commits consumer offsets in one Kafka transaction, ensuring both succeed together or both fail and re-deliver the batch.

_Part of [Exactly-once Kafka transaction for aggregates and offsets](exactly-once-transaction.md)_

When a batch of clicks arrives from [Ad click tokens and fraud checks](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md), the [`ClickAggregator`](ad-click-aggregation-and-billing.md) consumes them from the `ads.clicks` topic. It groups the clicks by campaign and minute with [`aggregateBatch`](ad-click-aggregation-and-billing.md), counting valid and invalid clicks in each bucket. Then it opens a Kafka transaction. Within that transaction, it sends all the minute aggregates (each keyed by campaign id) to the `ads.click-aggregates` topic, and tells Kafka to commit the consumer group's offset for the batch—the position where the next batch will start. If all of this succeeds, the transaction commits. If anything fails mid-way (a network error, a producer timeout), the entire transaction aborts: no aggregates are visible, and the offsets stay unchanged, so the batch is automatically re-delivered on the next poll. This atomic pattern ensures exactly-once delivery: every click in the batch is counted in exactly one aggregate, never skipped and never duplicated, even if the service crashes in the middle.

**Look at:** [`ClickAggregator` in click-aggregator.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/infra/click-aggregator.service.ts#L43)

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| queue | `ads.clicks` | Consumed: click records published by {{ad-click-tracking-and-fraud}}, grouped into batches by the consumer |
| queue | `ads.click-aggregates` | Published: minute aggregates grouped by campaign and minute, with source partition and first offset for idempotent re-writes |
| other | `ads-click-aggregator consumer group` | Committed atomically with each aggregate batch in the transaction; tracks the position in `ads.clicks` for re-delivery on failure |

## Watch out

- Transaction abort on error means failed batches are re-delivered automatically—not a manual retry in application code; the consumer will poll the same batch again from the old offset
- The idempotent keying is safe only because aggregates are keyed with `source_partition` and `first_offset`; otherwise re-writing the same batch would double-count clicks
- Consumer must use `readUncommitted: false` and `autoCommit: false` or the transaction pattern breaks—committed aggregates and offsets must stay perfectly in sync
- Transactional producer needs a unique `transactionalId` per instance (built from hostname + pid) or fencing errors occur in multi-node setups
